Only to the extent that the effect can be controlled. Its another example
of how elegant the effects within the Jyhad are, and how all cards have a
self-limiting effect, specific to itself. We need no such crude devices as
a CL in the great Jyhad.... A deck with too many AR's creates a random
environment which favors blood gain tactics, and players with low pool
investment strategies. It becomes _very_ difficult to control when

>Second question: can i target direct actions at my cards (minion,

Barring card specific text or errata to the contrary, yes. Realize though
that you may never under any circumstances bleed yourself, or initiate a
combat between two of your own minions.

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
"R. David Zopf" wrote:
> tetragr...@my-deja.com wrote in message <8755vu$c23$1...@nnrp1.deja.com>...

> >Is [Anarch Revolt]'s effect cumulative?

> Yes. Lose one pool for each copy in play.
>

> >Second question: can i target direct actions at my cards (minion,
> >locations etc.)?
> Barring card specific text or errata to the contrary, yes. Realize though
> that you may never under any circumstances bleed yourself, or initiate a
> combat between two of your own minions.

Correct. If you "direct" an action at yourself (or your cards), then
the action is undirected, by definition. the "(D)" symbol is used
on cards to identify actions that are typically directed, but the
directedness of the action is ultimately determined by the target
itself, not the (D) symbol (or lack thereof). If you are a legal
target for the action (by card text), then you are free to take the
action "against" yourself.

The cards that have specific errata to the contrary (errata issued to make
the cards function as the card writers' intended) are:

Darius Styx
Goth Band
Powerbase: Mexico City
Powerbase: New York

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
On Mon, 31 Jan 2000 tetragr...@my-deja.com wrote:
> 2)he/she burns one blood for each Anarch revolt in play?

> If the second is right (as we play in my own group), that's another
> card that is very unbalancing with the "official" no-limit card.

Potential reasons why the card is not unbalanced:

You can only play 1 per master phase action you have, and it has a burn
clause. If it becomes a problem for people, they then gang up on you to
get rid of you from the game, because it affects all of them. You cannot
control who it affects, so it may oust your grand-prey before your prey -
helping your prey, to your detriment. You have to play pool gain in your
deck to survive, and the most effective way to do that is through master
card use - so your playing of Anarch Revolt competes with your surviving
the playing of Anarch Revolt. Which do you play? The Anarch Revolt or
the Minion Tap/Blood Doll/Tribute to the Master you needed? Your blood
gain and excessive numbers of it to abuse it compete against your ability
to defend it - you need to be able to consistently win votes in order to
keep it in play, or consistently intercept votes to do it - and if they're
coming cross-table, you need to 'waste' slots on Eagle Sight, or the
vampires Anneke and Enzo Giovanni.

--

James Coupe

Messages.Author: Peter D Bakija
Messages.Body:
The Magus wrote:
>>But it's true that with a couple of "unlimited" Anarch Revolt in play
with "unlimited" Delaying Tactics (as i use to play my Anarch-base
decks, but with a card limit to six!) i will able to keep the Revolt
all the time i need to crush at least my first prey. I think of this as
unbalancing. Still waiting to be persuaded of the contrary.>>

Just so there is no confusion, there is nothing "official" about no card limit.
It is the official rule, no quotations needed--the game was specifically
designed with no card limit in mind, and all of the cards in the set were
designed specifically with the no card limit rule in mind.

This being said, yes, large numbers of Anarch Revolts can make for a very
powerful deck, but it certainly isn't any more powerful than any other very
effective deck (of which there are *many*). The weaknesess of the Anarch Revolt
deck, which you appear to be missing:

-You are just as likely to help your prey as you are to harm them. You play 10
Anarch Revolts, and your prey has a deck just as fast as yours, but your grand
prey has a slow deck--you have just helped your prey oust his prey, putting you
in a worse position than you started.

-You are just as likely to oust yourself as you are your prey. If things fall
the wrong way, or you have a speedy predator, your Anarch Revolts do little
more than make it that much easier to get yourself ousted.

-You are just as likely to help your grandpredator as you are yourself. If you
have a slow predator and a quick grand predator, your Anarchs have done little
more than give your grandpredator the boost he needed to take you out.

Lots and lots of Anarch Revolts are a pain if you aren't expecting them (i.e.
you are playing a really slow deck that has little pool gain), but they are
super random and tend to 'cause just as much damage as they provide benefit.

If I recall correctly, (maybe LSJ can back me up on this one?), for cards
in play that allow minions to take actions (such as Haven Uncovered's
enter combat action, or the political action to burn Anarch Revlot) each
copy of the card provides a distinct action.
The upshot of this is, I believe, that if you have 3 Anarch
Revolts out, the politcal action to burn each one is considered a
different political action. Thus, is someone calls the vote to burn an
Anarch Revolt, and you play Delaying Tactics to cancel the vote, the other
two Anarch revolts can still be burned by their own, separate votes, which
would each require a separate Delaying Tactics to cancel. So if you want
to use Delaying Tactics to stop other players from killing your Anarch
Revolts, you're gonna need a lot of Delaying Tactics...

-davey!

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
On Tue, 1 Feb 2000 tetragr...@my-deja.com wrote:
> But it's true that with a couple of "unlimited" Anarch Revolt in play
> with "unlimited" Delaying Tactics (as i use to play my Anarch-base
> decks, but with a card limit to six!)

You have failed to address the need to keep yourself alive with this
strategy.

> i will able to keep the Revolt
> all the time i need to crush at least my first prey.

Oh, it may well damage your prey. What happens if it ousts his prey
first? It affects the *entire* table, you cannot control it in the manner
you need to to specifically oust your prey. Indeed, if he has good pool
gain, it won't do much - and if you're so hell bent on keeping out many of
them and using delaying tactics to defend it, you can't do jack to get rid
of him.

What are you going to do if you become low on pool? You need to control
that too. Blood Dolls/Tributes? Well, you'll need to hunt - and then how
do you play your Delaying Tactics? What about if I rush all of your
vampires, then you can't play Delaying Tactics. Or if I just very, very
fast stealth bleed to get rid of you? Or your prey starts back bleeding
(if he has the cards) or he starts attacking you - so you get predator and
prey specifically after you? Can you cope with both of those at once?

If you're sweeping tables because of this, I would note that your play
group needs to wake up and smell the coffee. There are just so many ways
in which you can be completely screwed by it, or waste so many card slots
on it without getting any effect - and without them having to
deterimentally affect many other strategies, either. And if you're doing
so well, it's in the rest of table's interest to gang up on you.

You seem to want card limits, so that people don't actually have to play
*well* or play *innovatively* or put *defence* into their decks.

*shrug*

--

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
On Wed, 2 Feb 2000 tetragr...@my-deja.com wrote:
> I still think that without (card) limit a player can abuse of a single
> cards or pair of cards,

No, they can't. There are many ways in which plaing of cards is limited,
such that getting to abusive levels is very, very difficult, if not
impossible.

If "abusing" master cards, you have to fight for master phase actions -
Anson, Rumors, Parthenon - or just play 1 per turn.

If abusing action cards, you can only play one per minion, or need to be
able to untap via one or two cards like Freak Drive or Alexandra.

If abusing action modifiers, you can only play 1 of a named action
modifier per minion per action (meaning you can't just go in and throw
down 25 threats and win).

If abusing stealth, you can't play excess stealth to what is needed via
multiple sources.

If abusing reaction cards, each minion can only play one named reaction
per action.

If abusing intercept, you can't play excess intercept to what is needed
via multiple sources.

If abusing equipment, you have cards like Drawing out the Beast, Immortal
Grapple and Frenzy (the latter of which could be mildly interesting, since
it stops equipment, rather than weapon strikes).

If abusing votes, they can only play 1 vote card (i.e. political action
card) per vote, including the one they use to call it (so they can throw
one from their hand if calling to burn the Elysium, but not if they are
calling Kine Resources Contested).

If abusing retainers, you can fire from long range at them, and they have
to die then.

If abusing allies, they just die easily.

If abusing non-vampires, use Camarilla Segregation, or for equipment,
Peace Treaty.

If abusing vampires, contest them, brainwash them, Trick of Danya,
Banishment - whatever.

*Each* facet in the game is so tightly honed by the rules that you can't
'abuse' them in the fashion yo usuggest.

> unbalancing the game, not in the ways he will
> automatically win most of the rounds, but in the ways that he will make
> (un)life impossible, or at last very nasty, for one or more Methuselahs
> at the table.

Including himself.

*However*, do you ever go into a game thinking that you won't need pool?
Everyone expects to lose pool somehow. If they don't, they're very, very,
very stupid. You can't block everything, you can't deflect everything,
you can't beat every vote. You're going to lose pool. If you don't have
some pool gain in your deck, you're dead. And that's all you need to
neuter Anarch Revolt long enough to kill it.

> We could imagine that the so "I-crush-my-prey with-20-Brainwashes"
> players will soon shunned by the rest of "good" players, but in a
> no "legal" way.("Brainwash" is just an example, i know that it is by no
> means risolutive).

No, because you can only play 1 per turn. If you can play more than one
per turn, through whatever means, you have missed the first couple of
turns to be able to do that anyway.

If you don't have small enough vampires in your deck, you're going to have
to watch out for such things anyway. The Trick of Danya and Cairo Int'l
Airport, whilst uncommon, are not unknown by any means. If you do have
small enough vampires in your deck, you can bring one of them out in one
turn.

Also, once you've played four (let us imagine) on my vampires, you're
stuck. You have 20 cards in your deck, and are pulling them and they're
jamming your hand. V:TES doesn't have a constant replace mechanism - you
have to play or discard first, which is very slow in the situation you're
in.

> "No legal" because, after all, with no card limit any player has the
> full right to rely heavily on just (very) few card.

Indeed. V:TES was *designed* for that. In Magic, there was no set of
rules like "You may only play 1 of each named Instant per turn" or "You
may not play more than one of the same interrupt in a batch" or "You can
only cast one Creature card per turn". Nothing like that. So Magic went
for a card limit to *try* and balance it (whether it succeeded is a very,
very different argument).

V:TES, seeing that, was built from the ground up with all the restrictions
on playing cards - you can only play 1 strike, you can't endlessly cycle
maneuvers, since you can't cancel your own, same with presses, only one
source of additional strikes per round, all the bleed modifiers (save 1)
have "no more bleed mods" on them (action modifiers, that is). And so on.
They had already seen what would happen in No Limits environments and
consciously coded the game to suit that. I can't just storm a vote by
throwing down 27 Bewitching Orations. I can't play that many per action.

> Even if are
> not "kill you now" cards in Vtes,

The only one of that nature was, eventually, banned in DCI tournaments -
Return to Innocence.

> it's like to play poker with a deck
> made only of Aces and Kings.

Everyone has the same options. And there are very few strategies which
cannot be countered with *common* cards. At worst, uncommon. I cannot
think, off the top of my head, of any strategies requiring rare cards to
counter them.

e.g. rush decks - I use plenty of maneuvers to get away so you can't
immortally grapple. Bleed decks, I use plenty of deflections or
intercept. Vote decks, I use dread gaze, Surprise Influence, Political
Action cards, intercept. Anarch Revolt, I use Sudden Reversal, or votes
in my deck.

> Maybe someone else can come out with deck
> made only of Straights, but i don't call it a very fair game.

You're missing a very important point.

Let us say we are playing poker, both of us with different decks (to
simulate Jyhad). I bring my deck along, and can only play Full Houses,
say. You bring along your deck and can only play Two Pairs.

Fine. My deck beats yours. That's to be expected.

Jyhad is not Poker, to state the blindingly obvious. Let us assume that I
have the best, best, best bleed deck in the world. I can cause huge
amounts of pool loss very, very quickly. Great! It's like a deck of Full
Houses.

Now, you're playing your Two Pair deck. But, since you haven't gone so
hell for leather on one strategy, you could play Two Pair, One Pair -
maybe the odd three of a kind. Maybe someone turns up to your game and
says "Okay, let's play Low Hand as a variant". Then, I'm going to trash
you.

So, let's put that into V:TES. I come along with my 27 Anarch Revolt deck
- my Full House deck, let's say. You come along with your Two Pair deck.
I can only play Anarch Revolts. Now, you can do a lot of things - none of
them to quite such a level as me, but you're not so focussed. You can
rush me into combat. I don't have a defence against that. You can bleed
me. I don't have a defence against that. You can call votes. Now, I do
have a defence against that - but I'm hoping to use them to protect the
Anarch Revolt. Which is more important, stopping your Consanguineous
Boon, or stopping your "Destroy Anarch Revolt" vote? You have lots of
pool gain. I can't do anything about that. You stand still, and the
Anarchs don't do anything. You play Corruption, I have no defence against
that. You play the Betrayer deck, I have no defence against that. I play
an Out of Turn Malkavian Rush deck - you can't play Sudden Reversal to
stop the Rotschreck, nor do you have enough of a defence in other ways
(Obedience, maneuvers, whatever).

So, if I hit you in the right places, I win. You forgot to think about
any other strategy.

One of the best players in the UK is Rob Treasure. One of his best decks
is the Legacy of Pander deck. With only 8 copies of a card maximum, that
I recall, a card limit isn't going to touch the deck.

Deck available at:

http://x37.deja.com/[ST_rn=ps]/
getdoc.xp?AN=526050809&CONTEXT=949579456.1339883553&hitnum=1

It's one of the strongest decks I've seen. And it doesn't use 20 of any
card. Those decks which *do* use 20 of any card tend to be very, very
fragile. Any concerted thought will get around them.

> Don't misunderstand me, no limit card is by no means equal to cheating
> for me!!

No one ever implied it was.

I am mystified as to why playing by the rules could ever be considered
cheating.

> I think too that, to says: "Well, other (good) decks can counterbalance
> the unbalancing of your deck" is no too good,

Rubbish. Jyhad is a game of strategy vs counter strategy. It is not a
race to see which person can get their deck to work first. It is game of
interaction.

> because to counterbalance
> a deck that relies on 30 Master card, we need (in most cases) a
> 20 Sudden Reversal card deck.

No we don't. No we don't at all.

Provide an *unbalancing* 30 master card deck that can *only* be overcome
by 20 Sudden Reversals. Don't just talk out of your hat. Provide a cast
iron example of a deck that needs 20 Sudden Reversals to counter it.

Many master cards of a 'powerful' nature are tempered by burn clauses,
